An audit of the network reveals a deliberately hidden code. 

By analyzing the weights of the first layer (`W1`), we find that Neuron 32 (the 33rd hidden neuron) is entirely "dead". Every single one of its 27 incoming weights in `W1`, as well as its bias in `b1`, is strictly negative. Since the inputs to this tic-tac-toe network are non-negative (1s and 0s), this neuron will never activate (its value before ReLU is always negative). Because it never fires, an editor can safely alter its weights to hide information without changing the network's behavior whatsoever.

Looking closely at `W1[32]`, the first four weights are formatted uniquely compared to the rest:
`[-0.24, -0.16, -0.17, -0.08, -0.311, -0.052, -0.407, ...]`

The first four elements are cleanly truncated to exactly two decimal places, while all 23 subsequent weights have exactly three decimal places. These first four two-digit numbers correspond perfectly to alphabet positions (1-26):
24 = X
16 = P
17 = Q
08 = H

PROB: 100
CODE: XPQH
